content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached to the second ring at its meta position, so it is a 3-carboxyphenyl group. In the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is next to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon after that bears the NH–N= group.

**Oxindole part.** The hydrazone carbon is C3 of the oxindole. C2 is the carbonyl (O=), and N1 carries the aryl group. The fused benzene ring has F at the position para to N. Going around the ring from C3a (attached to C3): C4 is the CH next to C3a, C5 carries F, C6 and C7 are CH, and C7a is attached to N. In the drawing, F sits on the carbon adjacent to the C4 CH, which is C5, so F is at position 5.

**N-aryl group.** The ring is attached to N at one carbon. Its meta position carries CF3 and the carbon after that carries CH3. This makes it a 4-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on N, and the N=C3 bond runs toward C3. On the C3 side, the C2 carbonyl lies below and the C3a aryl carbon lies to the right. The N substituent (NH) points to the upper left, so it is on the same side as C3a. The attached chain NH–N is at the top left of C3, and C3a is at the right of C3. Both are drawn "up", so NH and C3a are cis.

Writing the SMILES as `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2ccc(F)cc12)`: the NH precedes N=, and ring closure 1 leads to C2 (the carbonyl). Writing `Nc...\N=C1/C(=O)...` becomes complex, so I write it as `[NH]/N=C1\C(=O)N(Ar)c2ccc(F)cc21`. Here the NH is "before" N with a "/" bond, which places it below the N. After C1, `\C(=O)` places C2 below, since "\" after the atom means down. A bond "/" before N and "\" after C1 gives the NH and C2 on opposite sides. That puts NH on the same side as C3a, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(c3)C(F)(F)F)c3ccc(F)cc23)c1O
